findings.title: The current runner consumes the explicit license query before the attempt latch

evidence.runner_lines: 382-391 perform LICENSE_PREFLIGHT/lmstat; lines 393-395 create ATTEMPT and set state.attempt
evidence.required_order: ATTEMPT must be durably consumed before the first license query or tool use
evidence.observed_order: lmstat -> return-code check -> budget check -> ATTEMPT.mkdir

findings.impact: A failed or repeated license preflight can occur outside the one-shot attempt ledger, contradicting the requested governance boundary.
findings.required_successor_fix: Move durable ATTEMPT creation/state transition before the sole lmstat invocation, then ensure every post-attempt exit seals exactly one failure or success namespace. Add AST/order and mutation coverage for license invocation reachability.

findings.title: Seven helper-body early-return mutations bypass core governance while the official checker accepts them
findings.impact: The 70/70 suite checks call-site presence/order but does not prove that the invoked authority, namespace, exclusion, tool, sealing, and publication helpers are live.
findings.required_successor_fix: Add helper-body AST reachability checks and independent early-return mutations; prove the governing effects are on every executable path, not merely present as dead text.

findings.title: The exact tool-budget checker can be bypassed by uncounted or faked subprocess calls
findings.impact: The counters can remain 1/1/1 while the runtime issues zero or multiple license/simulation subprocesses; source-text counter cardinality is not call cardinality.
findings.required_successor_fix: Inventory subprocess call sites by AST/callee provenance, bind the sole lmstat/VCS/simv call to its corresponding increment and order, and reject any unaccounted subprocess capable of invoking these tools.

disposition: M1882 is not launchable. Do not create M1885 or M1886 and do not query a license or run VCS/simv/EDA. Preserve M1882 as failed source-review evidence; author an additive successor and subject it to a new different-author source review before any release chain.
